marks.gloss_en: דכיון דשרי להו מר ... טפי ופריק מעיקרא -- because of the market permission he redeems for more at the outset
since the master permits them to be sold, slaughtered and weighed in the market, he redeems for more at the outset
הנאתן דבעלים הוא -- after redemption the benefit is the owner's
reading 1: the clause speaks of after redemption -- the benefit of the sale is the Temple's
נשחטין? הא בעי העמדה והערכה -- scoped at 31b.3: הניחא למאן דאמר לא היו בכלל, אלא למאן דאמר היו בכלל מאי איכא למימר
reading 2: the clause speaks of before redemption
altar consecrations were not included in standing and valuation
reading 3: indeed after redemption, and 'their benefit is the Temple's' refers to the initial [redemption]
והתניא: the tithe is not sold, alive or slaughtered, unblemished or blemished
the baraita: of the firstborn it says 'you shall not redeem', and it is sold alive
Rav Sheshet: the mishna speaks of orphans' tithe, permitted because of returning a lost item
Rav Sheshet: the mishna speaks of the animal tithe of orphans
מכלל דגדול בהבלעה לא? מאי שנא מהא דתניא ... ואמר רב הונא מבליע לו דמי אתרוג בלולב
the baraita: one who buys a lulav from another in the sabbatical year -- he gives him the etrog as a gift, since he may not buy it in the sabbatical year
there the matter is not evident; here it is evident
the stam: there the matter is not evident; here it is evident
אם כן, מעשר בהמה תרי זימני למה לי?
Rava: this is what it says -- orphans' tithe is sold in the ordinary way; an adult's tithe that he slaughtered is sold by inclusion in its hide, fat, sinews and horns
the stam's reading of the mishna: what is excluded is sale in the market, so at home they are sold -- the tithe too?
Rav Idi heard it from Rav Sheshet, said it in the study hall and did not say it in his name
RaShBY: any scholar in whose name a teaching is said in this world -- his lips move in the grave
R' Yitzchak bar Ze'iri: the verse is 'moving the lips of the sleepers' -- like a heap of grapes, which flows when touched, so scholars' lips move when a teaching is said in their name
the baraita: the animal tithe of orphans -- one sells it; an animal tithe that one slaughtered -- one includes [its price] in its hide, fat, sinews and horns
Abaye: this is what it says -- the animal tithe of orphans is sold by inclusion
Rav Huna: if he did not want to give it as a gift, he includes the etrog's price in the lulav
Rava: from where do I say it? -- 'then it and its substitute shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed'
Rava's criterion: when does it make a substitute? -- alive; when is it not redeemed? -- alive
Rava: what is appraised while alive -- the rabbis decreed after slaughter; what is not appraised while alive -- they did not decree
